title: Content injection between Hits for React InstantSearch Hooks
body:
We recently published a guide on [how to inject custom content between hits](https://www.algolia.com/doc/guides/building-search-ui/ui-and-ux-patterns/injecting-content/react/), for React InstantSearch, and we'd like to gather interest in adapting this guide for React InstantSearch Hooks.

## What's Content injection between Hits?

Content injection consists of inserting data between search results. This pattern can be helpful for a variety of use cases:

- **Displaying promotional or editorial content** based on the search parameters, like the query or active refinements
- **Inserting promoted brand banners** between hits
- **Showing customized suggestions** based on the user profile

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/154633/151024389-b67a1bd2-f470-40b4-9c5f-4357b9596d36.png)

[**See Live Demo →**](https://zjp0h4.csb.app/)

## How to show your interest?

Simply add a "👍" reaction on this issue, and optionally subscribe to its notifications. We will share updates here.

We're specifically interested in injecting advertising banners, ideally from our CMS rather than via custom JSON in Algolia. 

After having a quick skim of the Composition docs the feature seems mainly to be used for injecting hits/results from the same index? Is that accurate? If so, do you have a recommendation for handling banners in React InstantSearch 7?

If you want to inject banners in a static position, I recommend an approach like https://www.algolia.com/doc/guides/managing-results/rules/merchandising-and-promoting/how-to/add-banners/ and inject it manually when you use `useHits` into the right position of the `items` list.

Thanks @Haroenv that's helpful. I'd been checking out the `useHits` documentation and had noticed the warning to not use `transformItems` to remove items as it would affect pagination. Would injecting the banner into `items` affect pagination too? 

We don't use infinite scroll and we have a grid layout that we want to keep looking nice and neat. I was wondering if we would need to modify `hitsPerPage` to ask for 19 items instead of 20 if we are showing 1 banner on the current page (for example), then reset it back to 20 when the user moves to a page without a banner? Can you think of anything else pagination-related that we'd need to handle? I was wondering if we'd have to use `offset`?

I've also been looking at the `algolia/algolia-react-boilerplate` repo, specifically https://github.com/algolia/algolia-react-boilerplate/blob/main/apps/boilerplate-front-end/src/components/hits/components/injected-hits/InjectedHits.jsx#L37 but I'm not sure if that approach is recommended or not, it's a bit of an old repo?

1. You can indeed do that, but for a page that's not the first page you'll be off by one hit then. I recommend you design a UI that doesn't change the number of hits requested per page if you're not using composition. You can't combine offset and length with page/hitsPerPage which InstantSearch uses. What you can do however is "translate" the page into an offset inside a search client interceptor
2. the other repository is an option, but because it's infinite hits it won't have your issue of needing to distinguish pages with injections and pages without

What you can probably do, to be able to use composition, is to put those banners as records in the index and ensure they are filtered out for the normal results. I'm not on that team so I don't know the exact features, but you can contact your CSM to get in touch with them.
